Practised drawing dot pictures for square and triangular numbers.
Used rows and columns to represent how a sequence grows.
Explored a 5-by-5 square as 25 dots.
Explained that a shared corner is counted twice and needs subtracting once.
Teach-back was not passed.
end.parentNote: Ishita practised showing square and triangular numbers with dot pictures and explaining how a new row or column changes a pattern. They used 5 × 5 = 25 and later clarified why a shared corner must be counted only once. At first, they mixed up the corner adjustment, but corrected the explanation later in the lesson. At home, ask them to draw a 3-by-3 or 4-by-4 dot square and mark the shared corner when adding a row and column.
